factory: Chateau Diadem factory (Santiago de los Caballeros)
about: A Dominican-made line from Chateau Diadem named after the Caribbean trade winds, using an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper in place of the habano 2000 on Conviction. It was introduced as a creamier, more affordable option in three sizes.
notes: The maker's strength scale shows medium for the Robusto 52 and Gran Toro and medium to full for the Corona Gorda, and its text calls the Gran Toro full bodied. The co-founder described the line to Cigar Journal as mild to medium. Launched at InterTabac 2026.
verifyNotes: Blend, factory and sizes match the maker page. Read the maker's strength bars from the page markup: Corona Gorda sits between medium and full, the other two at medium. Rewrote notes to say that. Body differs by size on the maker page (medium-full and full).

filler: Nicaragua (Esteli Criollo), Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Piloto Cubano)
factory: Chateau Diadem factory (Santiago de los Caballeros)
about: The debut blend from Chateau Diadem, the Dominican brand founded by cousins Emily Sahakian and Thierry Farah. It pairs an Ecuadorian habano 2000 wrapper with Dominican and Nicaraguan fillers and is rested six months before release.
notes: Sold in the US as Certitude because of a trademark issue; the cigars are the same. Strength is read from the maker's scale graphic, which sits between medium and full.
verifyNotes: All fields match the maker page and halfwheel. Maker strength graphic sits about 70 percent along the scale. Added the Cigar Journal article that supports the 2022 launch.

filler: Nicaragua (Esteli Criollo), Dominican Republic (Criollo 98, Piloto Cubano)
factory: Chateau Diadem factory (Santiago de los Caballeros)
about: The US-market name for Chateau Diadem's Conviction blend, renamed over a trademark issue. Apart from the name and packaging it is the same Dominican-made cigar with an Ecuadorian habano 2000 wrapper.
notes: Same cigar as Conviction, which keeps that name outside the US. Launched at PCA 2025 in six sizes.

factory: Chateau Diadem factory (Santiago de los Caballeros)
about: A single-size Chateau Diadem blend built around Connecticut Broadleaf in the filler under an Ecuadorian corojo wrapper. The company says it took nearly three years to develop and treats it as its showpiece cigar.
notes: The Connecticut Broadleaf is in the filler, not the wrapper. The maker describes it as full bodied. Launched at InterTabac 2026.
verifyNotes: No field changes. Maker strength bar sits between medium and full; the maker text says full bodied.

about: A collaboration between Chateau Diadem and blender Eladio Diaz, made at his Tabacalera Diaz Cabrera next door to the Chateau Diadem factory in Santiago. It comes in one robusto extra size and is aged a year before release.
notes: On sale in Europe since 2024 and in the US from PCA 2026. Cigar Journal's 2024 story called it a limited edition with a Dominican corojo wrapper and five fillers; the maker and halfwheel say Ecuadorian corojo and four Dominican fillers.
verifyNotes: No field changes. Trimmed notes slightly.

about: Chateau Diadem's value line: handmade medium-filler cigars sold in bundles of 10 in three sizes. The maker describes it as an everyday smoke at a lower price than its long-filler lines.
notes: Medium filler, not long filler. The maker does not publish the blend, strength or the three sizes.
verifyNotes: Maker page confirmed: it publishes no wrapper, blend, strength or size list. Could not look for a second source because web search was unavailable.

filler: Nicaragua (Esteli viso, Jalapa seco), USA (Pennsylvania viso)
about: The first line from Despot Cigars, built around four classic formats with one blend. Despot Cigars is the private label of Serbian brothers Jovan and Ugljesa Despot, rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
notes: The maker rates it medium to full, while Blind Man's Puff and US retailer Luxury Cigar Club call it medium. The factory is not disclosed. Blind Man's Puff lists its release date as April 2022.
verifyNotes: Blend, sizes and strength match the maker. Reworded the April 2022 note: Blind Man's Puff gives it as the release date and does not say it is the US arrival. Left released null because the maker's site predates that.

filler: Nicaragua (Jalapa volado, Esteli viso, Jalapa viso)
about: Despot's second line, blended for aroma over strength, with two short formats and two large traditional ones. Despot Cigars is the private label of Serbian brothers Jovan and Ugljesa Despot, rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
notes: The maker lists an all-Nicaraguan filler. US retailer Luxury Cigar Club shows the Serie J blend with Pennsylvania filler on its Serie U pages. The factory is not disclosed.
verifyNotes: No field changes. The maker's two pages differ on the binder (H Ecuador Claro on one, H Ecuador on the other).

about: Despot's third line, using an Ecuadorian rosado wrapper over Jalapa and Ometepe fillers in two 54-ring formats and two large classic shapes. Despot Cigars is the private label of Serbian brothers Jovan and Ugljesa Despot, rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
notes: The factory is not disclosed and the maker publishes no specific tasting notes.

about: Despot's fourth and fullest line, adding Pennsylvania Broadleaf to the filler and filling in formats the earlier series lacked. Despot Cigars is the private label of Serbian brothers Jovan and Ugljesa Despot, rolled in Esteli, Nicaragua.
notes: The maker says the wrapper and binder are the same Habano 2000 from Ecuador. Its blend list names Jalapa and Condega fillers, while its longer description says Ometepe and Jalapa. The factory is not disclosed.

about: A limited edition from Despot Cigars made in honor of Cigar Lounge Libertador in Belgrade, Serbia. It uses an Ecuadorian habano claro wrapper and binder over Nicaraguan filler.
notes: The blend is close to Serie U. The maker does not publish the size, strength or release year.

about: The first limited edition from Despot Cigars, made as a tribute to its Serie J line. It is one large 7.5 by 52 cigar made with tobacco aged at least seven years.

about: The core range from EGM Cigars, a Swiss-based house led by Ettore Gabriele Moraschinelli. They are Dominican puros made with Cibao Valley tobacco in Cuban-style formats such as the Laguito sizes.
notes: The maker rates each size: Encantos light to medium; Petit Encantos, Robustos, Blecos and Diademas medium; Bravos, Escudos, Poderosos, Tiburones and Media Coronas medium to full. It names no leaf varieties or factory. Sizes are published in millimetres.
verifyNotes: All ten sizes match the maker's millimetre specs. Fixed the per-size strength list in notes (Tiburones and Media Coronas are also medium to full; Petit Encantos and Diademas are medium). about: EGM's first blend that is not a Dominican puro, putting an American-grown Broadleaf maduro wrapper over Cibao Valley binder and filler. It comes in three sizes and is rolled by hand in Santo Domingo.
notes: The maker says only American-grown Broadleaf; halfwheel identifies it as Pennsylvania Broadleaf and the factory as ABAM Cigars in Santo Domingo. The maker rates it medium to full, and halfwheel's reviewer put it closer to medium-plus. Sizes are published in millimetres.

about: The top line from EGM Cigars, a Dominican puro of aged Cibao Valley tobacco in three sizes with foot bands naming each vitola. It was unveiled in London in autumn 2025.
notes: An ongoing line, but the maker says it is made in very limited quantities. Sizes are published in millimetres (130 x 55, 145 x 57, 170 x 52). Praxedes is a pyramid and Paraisos has a pigtail cap.

about: A single long, thin 178 mm by 34 ring cigar from EGM that revives the old Ninfa format. It is a Dominican puro rolled by hand with Cibao Valley tobacco.
